title: WhatsApp Launches Bill Payments in India, Connecting 500 Million Users to 22,700 Billers
excerpt: Meta's messaging platform integrates Bharat Connect network for utility, insurance, and loan payments directly in-app.
body:
• WhatsApp launched bill payments in India on September 3, connecting users to 22,722 billers across 30 categories through the Bharat Connect (BBPS) network.
  • Supported bill types include electricity, gas, water, FASTag, insurance, credit card dues, and loan repayments, with payments via UPI, debit, or credit cards.
  • WhatsApp Pay processed 150 million transactions in June 2026, up from 37 million in June 2024, though its UPI market share remains under 1%.
  • The feature is rolling out gradually across Android and iOS, positioning WhatsApp as a direct competitor to Google Pay and PhonePe in recurring household payments.

WhatsApp launched a bill payments feature in India on Thursday, September 3, allowing its roughly 500 million Indian users to find, manage, and pay household and utility bills without leaving the messaging app.

The feature is powered by the Bharat Connect network — formerly known as the Bharat Bill Payment System (BBPS) — which is operated by a subsidiary of the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI). It gives users access to 22,722 billers across 30 categories, including electricity, gas, water, FASTag toll top-ups, insurance premiums, credit card payments, and loan repayments.

How It Works

Users can access bill payments by tapping the rupee (₹) icon at the top of the WhatsApp home screen. The system auto-fetches outstanding balances from registered billers, and users can pay using UPI, debit cards, or credit cards.

WhatsApp has designed the feature around recurring household use. Bills from previously paid providers appear on the Payments Home screen for one-tap access, and users can manage multiple accounts under a single biller — allowing them to track bills for home, office, and family in one place. Frequently used categories surface automatically, with a "see all" option for the full list of 30-plus categories.

Meta's Growing Payments Footprint in India

The launch represents a significant expansion of WhatsApp's financial services in India, where the platform already supports mobile recharges, metro ticket bookings across cities, and citizen services through government chatbots.

"For millions of Indians, WhatsApp is already the simplest way to stay close to family and friends, talk to businesses, access citizen services, and buy everything from metro tickets to insurance — all without leaving the app. With Bill Payments, we're bringing that same simplicity to one of the most routine tasks in every household."

— Arun Srinivas, Managing Director and Country Head, Meta India

WhatsApp Pay processed 150 million transactions in June 2026, a fourfold increase from 37 million in June 2024. Its share of UPI transaction volume climbed to about 0.7%, up from 0.27% two years earlier — still a fraction of the market dominated by Google Pay and PhonePe, which together handle over 80% of UPI payments.

Targeting Recurring Payments

By choosing utility and household bills rather than peer-to-peer transfers as its entry point, WhatsApp is targeting a segment that processes roughly $15.6 billion worth of transactions monthly through the BBPS network. Recurring bills are a particularly sticky use case — once a user sets up their billers, they are likely to return each billing cycle, building long-term engagement.

The move also places WhatsApp in direct competition with Google Pay, PhonePe, and Paytm, all of which already offer BBPS-powered bill payments. WhatsApp's advantage lies in its installed base — it is India's most widely used messaging app — and the low friction of paying from within a familiar interface.

What's Next

The feature is rolling out gradually and will be available to all Android and iOS users over the coming weeks. WhatsApp did not disclose whether it plans to add auto-pay or bill reminders, features that competitors already offer.

For the Indian diaspora, the integration could simplify remote bill management for family members back home — paying a parent's electricity bill or managing FASTag top-ups from abroad, all within WhatsApp.
